llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (building and running multi-step workflows) matches the instructions it contains; there are no surprising installs or requested credentials, but the usual runtime risks of executing user-provided workflows (especially exec steps) remain and should be managed by the user.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with the SKILL.md: it describes building, persisting, and running workflows with API/agent/exec steps and branching. The referenced companion skills (smart-api-connector, setup-doctor, etc.) are plausible dependencies for that functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly cover creating, saving, reading, and executing workflows (including running shell commands via exec steps). They recommend safety checks (dry run, user confirmation, forbid obvious destructive commands). The SKILL.md does not hardcode storage paths or list exactly which environment variables it might read when users choose to use env vars; that is expected for a generic workflow tool but means runtime behavior depends on the agent/tooling environment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — nothing is written to disk by the skill itself during install. This minimizes supply-chain risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials in the registry metadata, and SKILL.md warns against embedding secrets and suggests using environment variables or a secure key store. Because it may read workflow files and (by design) use env vars or other skills' secure storage at runtime, users should ensure those runtime secrets are managed safely; the skill itself does not request broad credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomous invocation are appropriate. The skill does not request persistent system privileges or modify other skills' configs in the instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and matches its purpose, but it can execute shell commands specified in workflows. Before installing or running workflows: only run workflows you or trusted parties authored, perform dry runs, require explicit confirmation before any exec step, avoid embedding secrets in workflow JSON, and consider running workflows in a restricted user account or container. Also verify where workflow files will be stored on your system and confirm the agent's exec tool enforces the stated destructive-command checks.
